body:
Maria: quick sync — ran into a weird perf/fallback issue during a hosted->dedicated failover today, wondering how we want to codify the ownership and telemetry semantics
Ajay: details? what failed exactly? :thinking:
Maria: customer traffic hit a capacity threshold, smart-routing kicked in to fallback to dedicated variant, but latency spiked 3x for first few requests
Dina: first request coldstart? or credential hop?
Maria: looks like a combination. dedicated pool required a tenant credential rebind step that did a round-trip to private KMS and we also lost some prefix cache hints when switching runtime adapters
Sam: ugh, so two separate handoffs — token rebind + cache rebuild. can we decide which one is the responsibility of the control plane vs adapter?
Ajay: my take: control plane should guarantee atomic switch semantics for routing decisions (i.e., route switch is coordinated), runtime adapters own local caching and fast rebind heuristics. but we need a contract for expected bounding of rebind latency
Taylan: agree, and we should standardize an optional prefetch API: control plane can send a "prepare-handOff" with short-lived bootstrap creds to the target adapter so it can warm caches + establish KMS session before traffic arrives
Dina: prep API sounds useful. tradeoff: prep increases surface area for leaked credentials and complexity in private deployments where we can't push pre-credentials across network boundaries
Maria: exactly — private customers may not allow pre-priming. we need a policy flag on the manifest: allow_prefetch = [always|consent|never]
Ajay: implementable. also need observability: telemetry must include a handoff-signal so ops can correlate the latency spike with the exact step (token_bind, cache_miss, kernel_warmup)
Sam: current telemetry loses tenant identity when crossing hosted->private boundary due to anonymization rules. we should emit a handoff_id that is consistent but opaque (hash) so downstream sinks can join spans without leaking PII
Taylan: handoff_id + step-tagging is good. proposal: each routing decision increments a handoff_id and control plane attaches a signed handoff header to the first few requests so adapters can log the same id
Dina: signed header will fail in private/offline installs unless we provide a local signing key. maybe the adapter can generate the id and echo it back to control plane via the probe channel once it's ready
Ajay: meh, that loses correlation if the first request already timed out. prefer signed header from control plane when allowed, otherwise fallback to adapter-generated id and best-effort join
Maria: ok summary: 1) new manifest flag allow_prefetch with three modes, 2) control plane may optionally send prepare-handOff bootstrap creds when allowed, 3) telemetry should include handoff_id + step tags, signed header when possible, adapter-generated fallback otherwise
Sam: and we should document expected SLOs for each step (e.g., token_bind <= 150ms if local KMS, <= 800ms if remote KMS), so product teams can set realistic latency budgets
Taylan: add to RFC follow-up: sample config snippet for manifest and telemetry field names. also include migration plan for existing manifests (default to consent)
Dina: security note: ensure bootstrap creds are short lived (TTL < 1m) and audited to audit-sink regardless of mode
Maria: thanks — i'll draft a short RFC with the sequences, sample headers, and the manifest fields. assigning follow-ups: Ajay for probe API sketch, Taylan for telemetry schema, Dina for security review, Sam for SLO numbers
Ajay: on it, will post a prototype probe API this week
Taylan: will mock telemetry JSON and example dashboards
Dina: will draft the audit and key-rotation constraints
Sam: will run perf sims once Ajay's probe API lands
infra-bot: canary deployed routing-probe v0.1 to staging (build 2026.03.22-1912) :rocket:
Maria: awesome, thanks team :thumbsup:
